answer: Weight should follow endorsement diversity, not headcount. An identity gains influence only when vouched for by peers with disjoint histories: endorsements from one tight cluster collapse to a single knoll of support. Each endorsement carries a whisper of provenance, when it was earned and what work backed it, so recycled backing is easy to spot. A plume of fresh accounts with no independent past adds almost nothing. To fake influence, an attacker must cultivate many genuinely separate histories with sustained, checkable activity, making a Sybil farm cost as much as a real community.
